name: The Lantern Compact
description: A voluntary shelter network whose members disagree about who may hold a key.
missions: A refuge has accepted more guests than its blankets can warm. Its keeper refuses to sell the guest list.
A flood has exposed the names of old donors; a patron wants priority for their descendants.
The compact must decide whether the next keeper may close a door for rest.

name: The Salt Ledger
description: Harbor accountants who can make a debt legible or turn it into a weapon.
missions: A storm-damaged cargo has three competing owners and one surviving crew.
The ledger records a payment the sailor never received; the merchant asks for a quiet correction.
A new trade table must choose who can inspect its fees and who may refuse a bargain.

name: The Unbound Archive
description: Independent record keepers, unwilling to make every old account a command.
missions: Two foundry records disagree about a worker’s wage. Neither records their private life.
An apprentice has corrected the patron’s favorite translation in public.
The archive can protect several accounts or sell a single authorized version.

name: The Rootward Circle
description: Orchard keepers, charcoal burners and willing guides who argue over the forest’s changing edge.
missions: The new seed bed lies where an old tenant still gathers food.
A walking orchard has damaged a road; its keeper offers an ungainly but useful repair.
The circle has room for a shared route, a paid harvest or an exclusive claim.

name: The Ash Company
description: A company of adult veterans choosing between service, wages and another commander.
missions: A company chest contains fewer wages than its signatures promise.
A civilian relief wagon asks to cross a disputed military toll.
The next company charter can limit service or bind households to an armed patron.

name: The Quiet Table
description: Private messengers and discreet traders; secrecy may protect a person or conceal coercion.
missions: A sealed parcel belongs to a living recipient who may decline it.
A collector offers money for a courier’s private route.
A hidden meeting place needs a rule about who may bring an unwilling guest.
